Werner Herzog once said that seeing a piece of fried bacon stuck to a bathroom wall in Gummo completely knocked him out of his chair. A random, almost absurd image but somehow unforgettable. That’s exactly the kind of film this is.

Directed by Harmony Korine, Gummo doesn’t follow a proper story. It just drifts through a small, tornado-hit town, showing random slices of life. Kids hanging around, strange routines, moments that feel real but also a bit off.

It’s messy, uncomfortable, and not for everyone. Some people hated it when it came out, others saw something completely different in it. Over time, it built a cult following and inspired a wave of indie filmmakers who weren’t afraid to break the rules.
